page2_img_1.png.title: Bar chart of demographics and work-practice yes/no percentages
page2_img_1.png.description: Stacked horizontal bars show the share of respondents answering Yes (light) or No (dark) for nine demographic/work-practice items (N=797). Key values: 29% are in test vs 71% not; 15% are managers/leads; 75% majored in computer science (25% did not); 7% work remotely and 7% work on games (93% do not); 81% use Stack Overflow; 64% code in their spare time; 63% listen to music while working; 77% have built a tool; and 19% have any monitor in portrait orientation. The legend at the top identifies dark bars as “No” and light bars as “Yes,” highlighting that most respondents are local, CS‐trained engineers who actively use community resources and often create tools or code outside work.

page3_img_1.png.title: Table of statistically significant personality differences by question
page3_img_1.png.description: A table listing non-personality survey items (demographics, work practices, beliefs) that show statistically significant differences in Big Five trait scores; each row names the trait, the group means (normalized to mean=25, sd=5), and marks differences that remain significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction with **. Examples shown: managers score higher on Conscientiousness (No: 24.74, Yes: 26.55 **) and Extraversion (No: 24.82, Yes: 26.17); respondents who use Stack Overflow (Openness No: 23.54, Yes: 25.33 **) or who code in spare time (Openness No: 24.05, Yes: 25.54 **) have higher openness; engineers who built a tool score higher on Conscientiousness (No: 23.69, Yes: 25.40 **) and lower on Neuroticism (No: 25.86, Yes: 24.74). Belief-related differences include higher Extraversion for those who agree “Agile development is awesome” (Disagree: 23.09, Neutral: 24.56, Agree: 25.62 **), and greater Openness among those who prefer distributed version control (Agree: 26.01 **).

page2_img_2.png.title: Stacked-bar distributions of developers' beliefs on practices and workplace
page2_img_2.png.description: A horizontal stacked‑bar chart showing percentage responses (Disagree / Neutral / Agree) to 12 belief statements from the survey. Strong consensus items include: “Code reviews make code better” (about 93% agree), “There is no one size fits all approach” (~90% agree), “I like my manager” (~84% agree), and “Developers should test their own code” (~84% agree); similarly, 84% disagree that “Comments are not useful,” and 61% disagree that “Design patterns hurt design.” Several items show lack of consensus: “Static typing is better than dynamic typing” is split (≈12% disagree, 42% neutral, 46% agree) and choice of version control is mostly neutral (≈51% neutral, 37% agree distributed), while “Open workspaces are more productive” is contested (≈52% disagree, 25% neutral, 23% agree). The chart therefore highlights where developers largely agree (reviews, testing, no single approach) versus where opinions are mixed (typing, version control, open offices).
